text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 9 in history:
1386 - The Treaty of Windsor was signed under which England and Portugal pledged their permanent alliance and friendship.
1502 - Christopher Columbus set out from Cadiz, Spain, on his fourth and last voyage.
1657 - William Bradford, pilgrim father and governor of Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts for 30 years, died.
1671 - Thomas Blood, Irish adventurer better known as Captain Blood, stole the crown jewels from the Tower of London.
1785 - British inventor Joseph Bramah patented the beer-pump handle.

1800 - John Brown, militant U.S. anti-slavery campaigner, born. In 1859 he seized the Federal arsenal at Harpers Ferry, Virginia, hoping to encourage an uprising of slaves. No response came and federal troops recovered the arsenal.
1805 - Johann Christoph Friedrich von Schiller, German romantic poet and playwright, died.
1850 - Joseph-Louis Gay-Lussac, French chemist and physicist, died. He established the fact that all gases expand equally with heat.
1873 - Howard Carter, British archaeologist, born; he discovered the tomb of King Tutankhamen in Egypt in 1922.
1901 - Australia opened its first parliament in Melbourne.
1926 - Americans Richard E. Byrd and Floyd Bennett became the first to fly over the North Pole.
1927 - Canberra replaced Melbourne as the capital of Australia.
1931 - Albert Michelson, U.S. physicist who established that light has a constant speed, died. In 1907 he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics.
1936 - Ethiopia was formally annexed by Italy.
1945 - Final surrender documents were signed by Germany at the end of World War Two; German garrison in the Channel Islands surrendered.
1946 - King Victor Emmanuel III of Italy abdicated and the monarchy was replaced by a republic.
1949 - Prince Louis II of Monaco died shortly after delegating his powers to Prince Rainier, who began his reign on April 11, 1950.
1960 - U.S. became the first country to use the birth control pill legally.
1963 - A state of emergency was declared in British Guiana following a three-week general strike.
1967 - Dr Zakir Hussain was elected president of India.
1976 - Ulrike Meinhof, a leader of the Baader-Meinhof terrorist group, hanged herself in prison.
1978 - The body of former Italian prime minister Aldo Moro was found in the boot of a car; he had been kidnapped and murdered by the Red Brigade.
1979 - 18 people were killed when troops opened fire on terrorists occupying San Salvador cathedral in El Salvador.
1980 - Pope John Paul II and the Archbishop of Canterbury met for the first time in Ghana.
1985 - U.S. film actor Edmund O'Brien died. He won an Academy Award for best supporting actor in "The Barefoot Contessa" (1954) and was nominated for another Oscar for "Seven Days in May" (1964).
1986 - Sherpa Tenzing Norgay died; he shared with Edmund Hillary the achievement of being the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953.
1987 - A Polish LOT airlines Soviet-made Ilyushin 62 crashed in a wooded area outside Warsaw, killing all 187 on board.
1991 - William Kennedy Smith, nephew of Edward Kennedy, was charged with rape.
1993 - Paraguay held its first presidential and parliamentary elections for nearly 50 years.
1995 - World leaders concluded three days of emotional Victory Day celebrations across Europe with ringing calls for global reconciliation.
1996 - The National Party, which inflicted apartheid on South Africa then helped break the hated system, decided to quit Nelson Mandela's two-year-old government of national unity, effective June 30.
1996 - President Yoweri Museveni won a landslide victory in Uganda's first presidential election in 16 years.
